Strictly Come Dancing 2026 has reached its halfway point, with just 10 couples left in contention for the Glitterball trophy.
Following the elimination of Emmerdale star Lawrence Robb last week - after the show's first-ever bottom three dance off - the competition is tighter than ever, with six different couples topping the leaderboard so far.
Things are particularly tense at the bottom as Jaime Winstone, who has been in several dance-offs, will automatically make it through to the next round due to an injury in rehearsals.
This week's performances will see a smorgasbord of dances, including a Cha Cha by Delta Goodrem, a Rumba by Lacey Turner, a Quickstep by presenter Will Best and a Paso Doble by current favourite Tabby Stoecker.
Follow live updates below...
Jaime Winstone to miss tonight's episode
Actor Jaime Winstone is set to miss this weekend's shows after tearing an abdominal muscle.
The BBC announced the news on Wednesday (4 November), sharing that doctors have advised the actor to rest this week.
"In line with the rules of the show, Jaime and Carlos will receive a bye through to next week when it is hoped they will be able to dance again. We wish Jaime the very best as she continues her recovery," a spokesperson said.
Results show to honour Remembrance Sunday
With this week's results show occurring on Remembrance Sunday (8 November), Strictly will mark the occasion with a themed dance celebrating the women of the Second World War.
Has this series been a damp squib?
Our writer Rachel McGrath thinks so - from cruel new rules to teething issues with the hosts.

Strictly Come Dancing 2026 has reached its halfway point, with just 10 couples left in contention for the Glitterball trophy.
Following the elimination of Emmerdale star Lawrence Robb last week - after the show's first-ever bottom three dance off - the competition is tighter than ever.
Things are particularly tense at the bottom as Jaime Winstone, who has been in several dance-offs, will automatically make it through to the next round due to an injury in rehearsals.
This week's performances featured a smorgasbord of dances, including a Cha Cha by Delta Goodrem to a Jennifer Lopez hit, a Rumba by Lacey Turner, a Quickstep by presenter Will Best and a fiery Paso Doble by current favourite Tabby Stoecker.
Meanwhile, Dani Dyer's famous father, Danny Dyer, made a cameo as she and her professional partner Nikita visited the family's caravan park, before wowing the judges with their American Smooth and receiving their first "10" of the competition.
Dani and Nikita ended up topping the leaderboard with a total of 36 points, while John and Katya, Cach and Maddie came in joint last with 26 points each.
Follow live updates below...
And that's it for tonight! Here's the leaderboard for Week 7
Leaderboard for Week 7
Dani and Nikita: 36
Tabby and Mark: 33
Delta and Kai: 31
Lacey and Vito: 30
Bethany and Nancy: 30
Will and Dianne: 29
Graeme and Lauren: 28
John and Katya: 26
Cach and Maddie: 26
Dani and Nikita: comments and scores
There was more of a consensus from the judges for Dani and Nikita's American Smooth, with Shirley telling the reality star she should be "exceptionally proud" of herself.
Similarly Anton loved the pizazz and sparkle of the routine: "Well done you."
"I loved it," Craig said. "A classic American Smooth."
Scores:
Craig: 8
Motsi: 10
Shirley: 9
Anton: 9
For a total of: 36! Fantastic score
Next up: Dani and Nikita
Dani and Nikita fared well last week thanks to their Viennese Waltz to "My Favorite Things" from the Sound of Music... now they're hoping to impress with an American Smooth to one of my favourite things... Harry Connick Jr's cover of the American standard, "It Had to Be You" - which famously featured in the 1989 romcom When Harry Met Sally!
Cach and Maddie: comments and scores
Oh dear... the judges are really at odds with one another tonight! Craig actually called out professional dancer Maddie for her posture, yikes.
Shirley still thinks Cach is a frontrunner, so there's that...
Scores:
Craig: 4
Motsi: 8
Shirley: 6
Anton: 8
For a total of 26... will they be saved from the dance-off by the public votes?
Next up: Cach and Maddie
Cach and Maddie were joint third on the leaderboard last week with a not-to-be-sniffed at 33, after dancing the Argentine Tango to "Pas de Deux" by Michael Abels. This week they're waltzing to "That Ain't You" by Mulaa Jones, so we'll be looking for something sweeping, elegant and moving.
Tabby and Mark: comments and scores
The judges seemed much more in sync about that performance, "this girl came back with a vengeance!" Motsi proclaimed. "You are magnificent, I loved the focus."
Anton was a huge fan: "Yes! Yes! Yes! You are back on form."
Scores:
Craig: 7
Motsi: 9
Shirley: 8
Anton: 9
For a total of 33! Tabby is definitely back.
THIS IS WHAT WE NEEDED
OK, gawd this episode needed some drama, whoosh! Absolutely smashing performance already, super fiery, fierce expressions from Tabby and I'm loving the costumes. Bring it!!
Up next: Tabby and Mark with the Paso Doble
Tabby and Mark didn't manage to bewitch the judges last week, not even with their Quickstep to "Black Magic" by Little Mix. This week, they're dancing the Paso Doble to another old favourite of mine, "Supermassive Black Hole" by Muse (don't you dare judge me), here's hoping it gets Tabby and Mark out of their scoring slump.
Graeme and Lauren: comments and scores
It was an emotional one for Graeme as he reflected on a stroke he suffered in 2019, leading to doctors to discover a 13mm congenital hole in his heart. After undergoing surgery, he achieved a successful recovery.
The judges were suitably moved by Graeme's Couple's Choice dance, even if they all seemed to agree that it wasn't, as Craig put it, a "technical masterpiece". Craig did, however, praise Graeme's storytelling.
Scores:
Craig: 5
Motsi: 8
Shirley: 7
Anton: 8
For a total score of 28, so not the bottom of the leaderboard!
